canonical_object.statement: Every executing face in this profile roots in Apeiron.Table.HMap, Apeiron.Table.get, Apeiron.Table.insertWith and Apeiron.Table.build, together with Apeiron.Trichotomy.AnyRing.RingCell, Apeiron.Trichotomy.AnyRing.ringMul and Apeiron.Trichotomy.AnyRing.ringNormForm, with the extracted Cell<i64> word bodies word_mul_denote and word_norm_denote. A face that names the canonical object only by path, namespace or import is not rooted.
canonical_object.qualifier: The O(1) qualifier is fixed N, bounded callbacks and nonconstant key length; reading a whole source remains at least linear in its bytes at fixed N, so constant-time table operations at fixed N do not imply constant-time whole-source checking or constant-size proof terms.

seven_fields.name: 1 canonical object and observation relation with an exact scalar type
2 concrete entry points and source identity on each side
3 representation invariant established by the actual constructor
4 separate Rust and Song admission predicates
5 success / unsupported-input / resource-exhaustion behaviour with raw return encoding and post-state
6 separate Rust and Song resource accounting
7 source-connected refinement and a rejecting control

rows.title: Word arithmetic merge: the addition slice

canonical.object: The merge parameter f : V -> V -> V of Apeiron.Table.HMap; the arithmetic merge is commutative-ring addition on the scalar. Canonical observation: reading a built table at a key is a fold of f over that key's values in stream order.
canonical.observation_relation: Apeiron.Table.get (Apeiron.Table.build f d kvs) x = ((kvs.filter (fun kv => kv.1 = x)).map Prod.snd).foldl (fun acc v => f v acc) d (get_build_acc); schedule freedom under hcomm and hassoc (build_gauge_invariance).
canonical.scalar_type: Rust i64, wrapping Z/2^64 (i64 as Ring add = i64::wrapping_add); Song mergeAcc(left, right) = left + right on bounded machine integers with 0 <= left, right <= COORD_CEILING; canonical scalar ZMod (2^64) under denote.

song.role: pure accumulator merge with in-tree comm/assoc laws
executing MERGE_ACC arm computes oldVal + value inline

representation_invariant.constructor: Scalar arguments have no table constructor: their representation obligation is the input encoding and denotation. WordMerge is a stateless Rust instance; mergeAcc and the inline addition are operations, not constructors. Table-state construction belongs to R2.
representation_invariant.statement: A scalar is its i64 bit pattern. Rust wrapping add denotes addition in ZMod (2^64). Song mergeAcc(left, right) = left + right is that same addition on the matched bounded domain 0 <= v <= COORD_CEILING. Rust WordMerge and the Song inline oldVal + value are the canonical merge f only when the two additions agree on the matched domain; that agreement is not yet proved for the Song side.

rust.predicate: The merge admits every (i64, i64); i64 as Ring add is total wrapping. There is no merge-level refusal; admission is inherited from the table write (insert_with).

song.predicate: mergeAcc admits every pair. The inline addition in tableInsertWith executes only for an existing key with merge = MERGE_ACC, after capacity, key, merge-code and slot checks succeed. mergeAcc's law givens require 0 <= left, right <= COORD_CEILING; the inline arm carries no such guard.

behavior.success: mergeAcc is pure addition. In tableInsertWith, the inline addition executes only for an existing key with merge = MERGE_ACC, after capacity, key, merge-code and slot checks succeed. A fresh MERGE_ACC or MERGE_MAP insertion stores and returns value without addition; a fresh MERGE_SET insertion stores and returns 1. An existing MERGE_ACC insertion stores and returns oldVal + value; existing MAP and SET writes return value and 1, respectively.
behavior.unsupported_input: Rust: none at the merge; every pair is defined. Song: none at mergeAcc; a value outside 0..COORD_CEILING is outside the matched domain (the inline arm still computes).
behavior.resource_exhaustion: Not applicable at the merge: one addition either fits the word or wraps. There is no merge-level refusal.
behavior.raw_return_encoding: Rust an i64 word (wrapping). Song an i64-width word returned through tableSlotValSet; no separate success tag. A successful Song MAP or ACC write and a present-key read can also return -1.
behavior.post_state: Rust merge is pure (Merge::merge(&self, new, old) -> V). Song MERGE_ACC writes the merged value into the slot for an existing key; a fresh insertion stores value (or 1 under MERGE_SET) without addition; mergeAcc alone is pure.

rust.accounting: one wrapping addition per successful merge call

song.accounting: zero merge additions on a fresh ACC insertion and one on an existing ACC update; address, hash and probe arithmetic are additional costs

refinement.source_connected: Rust side: proof/Denotation.lean::denote_wrapping_add proves the wrapping word addition is ZMod (2^64) addition. The extracted WordMerge has no dedicated bridge theorem yet, so the Rust merge is source-connected to the canonical addition only through denote_wrapping_add, not through a table-level refinement. Song side: mergeacc_comm and mergeacc_assoc are in-tree Song laws, not canonical Lean, and no checked Song-to-Lean refinement exists. The joint refinement is OPEN.
refinement.rejecting_control: Change the Rust merge body from new.wrapping_add(old) to new.wrapping_sub(old) in a throwaway copy of src/table.rs, re-extract, and proof/regen.sh --check fails on the generated-body diff; restoring passes. This is an extraction-drift control; the semantic Song refinement remains the open obligation.

canonical.object: Apeiron.Table.HMap K V := K -> V with get, insertWith f k v m := fun x => if x = k then f v (m x) else m x, and build f d kvs.
canonical.observation_relation: get (insertWith f k v m) k = f v (m k) and get (insertWith f k v m) x = get m x for x != k; a built table reads as a per-key fold (get_build_acc).
canonical.scalar_type: Word instance Table I64 I64 WordHome 16: keys and values i64, denotation I64 -> ZMod (2^64); the physical home is home(key) mod 256.

song.role: probe for a key, returning slot or -1
probe for empty slot or matching key

representation_invariant.constructor: Rust Table::new(default, home) sets shards = [None; 256] and stores default; Song tableInit / tableInitGo writes key TABLE_EMPTY and value 0 into every slot.
representation_invariant.statement: Rust Rep(t, h): the fixed outer [Option<[Option<(K,V)>; N]>; 256], an untouched shard is None, globally unique keys, every entry in its home shard home(k) mod 256, and forall k, D(t)(k) = h(k) with D the matching override or the stored default. For the concrete I64 word instance the physical invariant is established at every fixed shard capacity N: emptyWordTableN_physicalInv establishes the real constructor and physicalInv_insert_with_all preserves it, including N = 0; get reads the represented total map; insert_with preserves PhysicalInv and canonical insertWith on success and returns the identical representative on ShardFull, with exact refusal at N = 0; for positive N, BuildAdmissibleN exactly characterizes build success versus ShardFull, table_build_physicalInv_of_buildAdmissibleN gives the successful-build PhysicalInv, and wordBuildN_zero_ok_iff_empty characterizes the zero-capacity build. The generic callback layer proves constructor, admitted insertion and admitted-build preservation under CallbackLawsG (insert_with_callback_admitted, table_build_physicalInv_of_buildAdmissibleG, table_build_zero_ok_iff_empty). word_table_new_rep remains the concrete read-only extensional relation forall key, word_table_get t key (value => value = h key) at Table I64 I64 WordHome 16, with canonical map type HMap I64 I64; it is the extensional component, not the physical invariant. A table-wide ZMod (2^64) representation theorem is not named here. Required Song invariant: an owned, valid extent of 2*cap memory cells; representable address calculations; unique occupied keys distinct from TABLE_EMPTY; probe reachability before the first empty slot; and an explicit denotation of occupied and absent keys. That invariant is over Song's represented storage, the caller memory[] extent, a different layer from the source-checker's memo store; no representation result transfers between the two without its own refinement. tableInit initializes the empty layout on valid memory. Constructor establishment, preservation and canonical denotation remain proof obligations for the Song side. Capacity validation alone does not validate the memory extent.

rust.predicate: Rust N = 0 is a supported zero-capacity configuration, not an unsupported input; writes return ShardFull. Full-capacity refusal requires an absent key. Existing keys can still update in a full Rust shard. Every explicit refusal occurs before any slot write and changes no field; earlier successful calls in a sequence remain visible.

song.predicate: On valid memory, Song tableInit returns 0 after initialization and returns -1 without writes for invalid capacity. tableFind returns a slot index or -1; tableGet returns the stored value or -1. Reads do not write. Every explicit tableInsertWith refusal occurs before slot writes and leaves the table unchanged; earlier successful calls in a sequence remain visible. Invalid memory/address extent and stack exhaustion have no checked refusal encoding in this profile.

behavior.success: Rust: Ok(()) with an existing key updating stored = merge(value, stored.clone()) and a new key inserting merge(value, default.clone()) in the home shard; N = 0 is a supported zero-capacity configuration, not an unsupported input, and writes return ShardFull. Song returns the stored value: a fresh MERGE_ACC or MERGE_MAP insertion stores and returns value without addition, a fresh MERGE_SET insertion stores and returns 1, an existing MERGE_ACC insertion stores and returns oldVal + value, and existing MAP and SET writes return value and 1.
behavior.unsupported_input: Rust: no table input is unsupported at this primitive; N = 0 is a supported zero-capacity configuration. Song: non-positive or non-power-of-two cap; key -1 (reserved); merge code outside MERGE_SET..MERGE_ACC.
behavior.resource_exhaustion: Rust: ShardFull exactly when the key is absent and the home shard has no vacant slot. Song: -1 when all cap probes are occupied. Existing keys can still update in a full Rust shard and a full Song table.
behavior.raw_return_encoding: Rust Result<(), StorageError>, StorageError::ShardFull; reads return &V. Song a raw word: -1 (TABLE_EMPTY) is overloaded across missing read, empty slot, invalid capacity, reserved key, invalid merge code and full table; a successful MERGE_SET write returns 1 (TABLE_PRESENT). Successful Song MAP or ACC writes and present-key reads can also return -1, so it is not merely a shared failure code (H1).
behavior.post_state: Rust refusal changes no field (word_table_shardFull_refusal at N = 16); success preserves the canonical insertWith denotation (open for arbitrary N). Song writes in place, so a mid-stream full table leaves earlier writes in place (H3); tableInit returns -1 on invalid capacity without writing.

song.accounting: zero merge additions on fresh ACC insertion and one on existing ACC update; address, hash and probe arithmetic are additional costs; initialization writes 2*cap memory cells
up to cap steps of tableLookupSlotGo / tableFindSlotGo, measure cap - step
0 allocated nodes; caller or static memory (the cells(32) test arena)

A separate composition task must specify Song's externally observable success and refusal post-state. A success-only restricted-domain result does not discharge B6's refusal/resource obligation.

hazards.statement: Song reserves key -1 (TABLE_EMPTY) and returns -1 for a missing read, while Rust has no reserved key and returns the stored default.
hazards.consequence: Song's raw return is not a reliable success/refusal tag: -1 conflates missing read, empty slot, invalid capacity, reserved key, invalid merge code and full table. Successful Song MAP or ACC writes and present-key reads can also return -1; it is not merely a shared code for several failures.

hazards.statement: Rust default is a stored value returned for any unwritten key; Song tableGet returns -1 for a missing key and has no stored default.
hazards.consequence: The matched observation relation remains OPEN. For additive fresh writes, Song stores value, whereas Rust stores value + default; equality under direct word observation requires default zero. But an absent Song read returns -1, whereas Rust then returns zero. Choosing default -1 fixes the direct absent-read comparison but breaks additive fresh-write equality. Excluding key -1 does not resolve this value mismatch. A state-aware observation/adaptation relation must be specified; no such relation is established here.

hazards.statement: Song tableInsertWith mutates slots in place; Rust build returns Err at the first refused insertion with no partial table.
hazards.consequence: Song's multi-insert is not transactional; a mid-stream full table leaves partial writes. This is the B6 composition obligation, not a shared semantics.

hazards.statement: Canonical I is S K K, while Song treats primitive i (TAG_I) and the normal form **skk as distinct (distinct_atoms, tag difference).
hazards.consequence: A regression fixture must pin the distinction; it is not something to patch away by conflating the primitive and the normal form.

hazards.statement: Song certcheck must refine Apeiron.Decider.checkCert and checkCert_sound.
hazards.consequence: Until that refinement exists, Song's UNSAT replay is not established as a refinement of the canonical checker.
